subject: Help to find out specific population type and questions related to my project

messages.author: 6a7541d8f5eaf783
messages.subject: Help to find out specific population type and questions related to my project
parts:
Dear Karl,

First of all, thank you for the time you spend providing support with your software.

I count with large population of individuals that were developed from homozygous founder lines over four generations of crosses. The crossing design is exemplified in the image, notice that all founders are different individuals. Two recombinant inbred lines were developed by selfing from each of some individuals of the last generation (G4). Although not considered for this analysis (yet), I count with SNP data from the individuals produced by outbreeding.

My aim is to reconstruct the founder haploblocks on the RIL genotypes. I could use some help on the best approaches:

- What should I set as the cross type? I assume it should end in 16 due to the number of founders, but should I choose riself16, genail16 or genril16?
- Could this protocol work for my purpose?: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/qtl2/html/maxmarg.html I understand that it finds the founder with maximum probability at each position
- I don't count with a genetic map. Could it be a limitation for calculating the genotype probabilities? If so, is there any way adjust the recombination rate?

Any help is appreciated. Best wishes :)

Jose

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Help to find out specific population type and questions related to my project
parts:
“riself16” matches this design, and so would be the preferred one. 
You could also use “genril16”. 

“genail16” would not apply, as it assumes a heterozygous population…that you did repeated outcrossing with no inbreeding.

The maxmarg() function is useful for identifying the most likely haplotypes. You can also try viterbi() though personally I prefer maxmarg().

You do need a genetic map, though if you have dense and informative genetic markers, it may not matter that much. But I would at least convert a physical map to estimated centiMorgans using some estimated recombination rate. You can, in principle, re-estimate the inter-marker genetic distances using est_map(), but it might be super slow in your case.

karl

I do have a very dense map. Actually, I have observed too many haploblocks to be detected in a single chromosome using the protocol from the link, even at high genotyping error probability. I will try to follow your advice :)

By the way, what is the default parameter of calc_genoprob() option map_function = c("haldane", "kosambi", "c-f", "morgan") ? I left this option blank as in the example.

All best,
Jose
